title: Lecture 9 · Electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation

blocks.html:
What to know

  • The chain passes electrons through complexes I–IV. NADH enters at complex I; FADH₂ enters at complex II. The energy released pumps protons from the matrix to the intermembrane space.
  • The proton gradient drives ATP synthase. Protons return through complex V, rotating it and phosphorylating ADP to ATP; this is chemiosmosis.
  • Oxygen is the final electron acceptor. It accepts electrons at complex IV and forms water. Without oxygen, the chain backs up and ATP production falls.
  • The yield is about 26–28 ATP per glucose. The exact number varies with shuttle use and proton leak; textbook values are approximations.
  • Uncouplers and poisons break the link. Uncouplers let protons leak across the membrane and release heat; cyanide and carbon monoxide block complex IV.

Check

check.question: What happens to ATP production when oxygen is unavailable?

options.text: The electron transport chain slows and ATP falls
ATP synthase reverses to make oxygen

check.explanation: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor. Without it, electrons cannot flow, the proton gradient collapses, and oxidative phosphorylation stops.
